title: Working from Home: The Real Trade-Offs

sentences.t: Working from home used to be a rare perk, but for millions of people it has become the new normal.
The question is no longer whether it works, but what it really costs us.
On the bright side, remote work saves time and money.
You skip the daily commute, you spend less on lunches and transport, and you can organize your day around your own energy levels.
Many employees also report being more productive, because there are fewer interruptions than in a busy office.
However, the picture is not entirely positive.
Without a clear boundary between work and home, the working day tends to stretch longer than anyone intended.
Casual chats by the coffee machine disappear, and with them go many of the small connections that make a team feel like a team.
So how can you make it work?
Start by creating a dedicated workspace, even if it is just a corner of a room.
Set fixed hours and stick to them, and take real breaks away from the screen.
Finally, make an effort to stay in touch.
A short video call or a quick message can do more for morale than you might expect.
In the end, working from home is neither a dream nor a disaster.
It is a tool, and the results depend on how deliberately we use it.
